title: Module quiz: Deployment architecture and data handling

questions.stem: Scenario: Marlow Care's service holds data of patients in the United States and in the European Union. It runs a deployment in each region. A European patient's request arrives while the European deployment is down for maintenance. What should the router do?

options.text: Decline to answer, and let the caller retry once the local site is back
options.says: Serving the user from another region breaks the residency requirement, so with no deployment that keeps the data in the region the answer is none.

options.text: Send it to the United States deployment, since being available matters more than where the data sits
options.says: Ruled out because "serving a European user from a United States deployment because it was available is the failure the router exists to prevent".

options.text: Send it to the European deployment that belongs to a different tenant, since the location still matches
options.says: Ruled out because another tenant's deployment breaks the tenant boundary: "one workspace per tenant".

options.text: Send it to whichever deployment answers the fastest, and record the exception in the audit log
options.says: Ruled out because speed is not a criterion, and the router sends a user's data "only to a deployment that keeps it in that region".

origin.section: Region: pin it where the platform lets you

questions.stem: Scenario: Alder Dental needs zero data retention on its Claude API deployment and has chosen a model that requires 30-day retention. What is the finding?

options.text: None, because the arrangement is organisation-wide and covers the models that are in use
options.says: Ruled out because the arrangement "excludes models that need 30-day retention" so it does not cover every model.

options.text: That choice cannot meet the target, so only a different one or another arrangement will do
options.says: A model that requires 30-day retention cannot meet a zero-retention requirement.

options.text: A warning only, since thirty days is short enough to be treated as nothing kept
options.says: Ruled out because the requirement is zero, and the page says the model "is part of the check".

options.text: None, provided the deployment's audit log is set to expire after thirty days
options.says: Ruled out because "the model is part of the check and not only the platform", and the audit log does not change what the provider retains.

questions.stem: Scenario: Wren Logistics must keep audit entries for at least 90 days and at most 365. An entry is 400 days old, and counsel has placed it under a legal hold. What does the purge rule do?

options.text: Purges it, because the ceiling applies to every entry alike
options.says: Ruled out because an entry under a hold "is never removed, whatever its age".

options.text: Purges the entry and keeps a copy for a further ninety days
options.says: Ruled out because the hold "keeps the entry itself and not a copy made at purge time", so nothing is removed first.

options.text: Retains it, because that order outranks the time limits
options.says: A legal hold keeps an entry whatever its age.

options.text: Retains it until the next audit closes, then purges it as usual
options.says: Ruled out because no audit date decides: "A hold ends only when counsel releases it".

origin.section: Retention has a floor and a ceiling
